claim: Spinally projecting serotonergic neurons play a key role in controlling pain sensitivity.
source: Spinally projecting serotonergic neurons play a key role in controlling pain sensitivity and can either increase or decrease nociception depending on physiological context.
evidence: This is a statement made in the abstract summarizing the role of these neurons.

claim: Spinally projecting serotonergic neurons can either increase or decrease nociception depending on physiological context.
source: Spinally projecting serotonergic neurons play a key role in controlling pain sensitivity and can either increase or decrease nociception depending on physiological context.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known property of these neurons.

claim: Two anatomically separated populations of serotonergic hindbrain neurons are located in the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi) and the medial hindbrain.
source: Utilizing virus-based strategies and Tph2-Cre transgenic mice, we identified two anatomically separated populations of serotonergic hindbrain neurons located in the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi) and the medial hindbrain, which respectively innervate the superficial and deep spinal dorsal horn and have contrasting effects on sensory perception.
evidence: This claim is supported by the tracing experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: LPGi serotonergic neurons innervate the superficial spinal dorsal horn.
source: Utilizing virus-based strategies and Tph2-Cre transgenic mice, we identified two anatomically separated populations of serotonergic hindbrain neurons located in the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi) and the medial hindbrain, which respectively innervate the superficial and deep spinal dorsal horn and have contrasting effects on sensory perception.
evidence: This is supported by anatomical tracing data shown in the figures.

claim: Medial hindbrain serotonergic neurons innervate the deep spinal dorsal horn.
source: Utilizing virus-based strategies and Tph2-Cre transgenic mice, we identified two anatomically separated populations of serotonergic hindbrain neurons located in the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi) and the medial hindbrain, which respectively innervate the superficial and deep spinal dorsal horn and have contrasting effects on sensory perception.
evidence: This is supported by anatomical tracing data shown in the figures.

claim: LPGi and medial hindbrain serotonergic neurons have contrasting effects on sensory perception.
source: Utilizing virus-based strategies and Tph2-Cre transgenic mice, we identified two anatomically separated populations of serotonergic hindbrain neurons located in the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi) and the medial hindbrain, which respectively innervate the superficial and deep spinal dorsal horn and have contrasting effects on sensory perception.
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic activation experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Serotonergic neurons of the LPGi are much more susceptible to transduction with spinally injected AAV2retro vectors than medial hindbrain serotonergic neurons.
source: Our tracing experiments revealed that serotonergic neurons of the LPGi were much more susceptible to transduction with spinally injected AAV2retro vectors than medial hindbrain serotonergic neurons.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the quantification of labeled neurons in different hindbrain regions.

claim: Activation of LPGi serotonergic projections decreases thermal sensitivity.
source: Taking advantage of this difference, we employed intersectional chemogenetic approaches to demonstrate that activation of the LPGi serotonergic projections decreases thermal sensitivity, whereas activation of medial serotonergic neurons increases sensitivity to mechanical von Frey stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data from chemogenetic activation experiments.

claim: Activation of medial serotonergic neurons increases sensitivity to mechanical von Frey stimulation.
source: Taking advantage of this difference, we employed intersectional chemogenetic approaches to demonstrate that activation of the LPGi serotonergic projections decreases thermal sensitivity, whereas activation of medial serotonergic neurons increases sensitivity to mechanical von Frey stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data from chemogenetic activation experiments.

claim: There are functionally distinct classes of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that differ in their anatomical location in the hindbrain.
source: Together these results suggest that there are functionally distinct classes of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that differ in their anatomical location in the hindbrain, their postsynaptic targets in the spinal cord, and their impact on nociceptive sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined anatomical and functional data.

claim: Functionally distinct classes of serotonergic hindbrain neurons differ in their postsynaptic targets in the spinal cord.
source: Together these results suggest that there are functionally distinct classes of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that differ in their anatomical location in the hindbrain, their postsynaptic targets in the spinal cord, and their impact on nociceptive sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing showing different laminar innervation patterns.

claim: Functionally distinct classes of serotonergic hindbrain neurons differ in their impact on nociceptive sensitivity.
source: Together these results suggest that there are functionally distinct classes of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that differ in their anatomical location in the hindbrain, their postsynaptic targets in the spinal cord, and their impact on nociceptive sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data showing opposite effects on pain sensitivity.

claim: LPGi neurons give rise to global and bilateral projections throughout the rostrocaudal extent of the spinal cord.
source: The LPGi neurons that give rise to rather global and bilateral projections throughout the rostrocaudal extent of the spinal cord appear to be ideally poised to contribute to widespread systemic pain control.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing data showing widespread spinal projections.

claim: LPGi neurons appear to be ideally poised to contribute to widespread systemic pain control.
source: The LPGi neurons that give rise to rather global and bilateral projections throughout the rostrocaudal extent of the spinal cord appear to be ideally poised to contribute to widespread systemic pain control.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical projection pattern and functional effects.

claim: Descending pain control is a critical endogenous mechanism of pain modulation that is required for survival.
source: Descending pain control is a critical endogenous mechanism of pain modulation that is required for survival (Millan, 2002), and allows an organism to respond in an appropriate context-dependent manner to external threats.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Descending pain control allows an organism to respond in an appropriate context-dependent manner to external threats.
source: Descending pain control is a critical endogenous mechanism of pain modulation that is required for survival (Millan, 2002), and allows an organism to respond in an appropriate context-dependent manner to external threats.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Key brain structures involved in descending pain control include the periaqueductal grey matter (PAG) and the rostroventromedial medulla (RVM).
source: Key brain structures involved in this system were discovered through stimulation-produced analgesia experiments and include the periaqueductal grey matter (PAG) and the rostroventromedial medulla (RVM) of the hindbrain (Basbaum and Fields, 1984).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The descending pain control system acts to inhibit the flow of nociceptive information through the spinal dorsal horn.
source: This descending system acts to inhibit the flow of nociceptive information through the spinal dorsal horn and requires descending tracts within the dorsolateral funiculus to mediate its effects (Basbaum et al., 1976; Basbaum et al., 1977).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The descending pain control system requires descending tracts within the dorsolateral funiculus to mediate its effects.
source: This descending system acts to inhibit the flow of nociceptive information through the spinal dorsal horn and requires descending tracts within the dorsolateral funiculus to mediate its effects (Basbaum et al., 1976; Basbaum et al., 1977).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The RVM is required for maintaining some chronic pain states through a process of descending facilitation.
source: The RVM is also required for maintaining some chronic pain states through a process of descending facilitation (Porreca et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2009), indicating that this area has a bidirectional control over pain sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The RVM has a bidirectional control over pain sensitivity.
source: The RVM is also required for maintaining some chronic pain states through a process of descending facilitation (Porreca et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2009), indicating that this area has a bidirectional control over pain sensitivity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited literature showing both inhibitory and facilitatory roles.

claim: Serotonin can inhibit nociception when injected intrathecally.
source: Monoamines are important neurotransmitters involved in descending pain control, with serotonin (5-HT) being able to inhibit nociception when injected intrathecally (Wang, 1977).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Spinal 5-HT contributes to stress-induced analgesia.
source: Spinal 5-HT is also known to contribute to certain forms of endogenous pain suppression, such as stress-induced analgesia (Yesilyurt et al., 2015) but is also required to maintain chronic pain in rodent models of nerve injury (Wei et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Spinal 5-HT is required to maintain chronic pain in rodent models of nerve injury.
source: Spinal 5-HT is also known to contribute to certain forms of endogenous pain suppression, such as stress-induced analgesia (Yesilyurt et al., 2015) but is also required to maintain chronic pain in rodent models of nerve injury (Wei et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Pain facilitation in pre-clinical neuropathy models is thought to be a result of reduced tonic diffuse noxious inhibitory controls, due to increased spinal 5-HT3 receptor activation.
source: This pain facilitation in pre-clinical neuropathy models is thought to be a result of reduced tonic diffuse noxious inhibitory controls, due to increased spinal 5-HT3 receptor activation (Bannister and Dickenson, 2016; Bannister et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The variety and abundance of 5-HT receptors within the spinal dorsal horn likely explains why multiple effects of serotonin are observed.
source: The variety and abundance of 5-HT receptors within the spinal dorsal horn likely explains, at least in part, why these multiple effects are observed (Bardoni, 2019).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: AAV2retro serotype may not infect serotonergic hindbrain neurons as efficiently as other descending projections.
source: However, it has been reported that the AAV2retro serotype, may not infect serotonergic hindbrain neurons as efficiently as other descending projections (Tervo et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Studies employing transsynaptic neuronal circuit tracing from dorsal horn neurons with modified rabies viruses rarely found labeled hindbrain serotonergic neurons.
source: Further, despite the dense serotonergic innervation of the spinal dorsal horn, studies employing transsynaptic neuronal circuit tracing from dorsal horn neurons with modified rabies viruses rarely found labeled hindbrain serotonergic neurons (François et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: It is possible that rabies-virus-based tracers fail to detect functional connections between serotonergic neurons and starter populations within the spinal cord.
source: This is surprising since both descending serotonergic neurons and dorsal horn interneurons are known to strongly influence nociception, and it is possible that these rabies-virus-based tracers fail to detect functional connections between serotonergic neurons and starter populations within the spinal cord.
evidence: This is speculation based on the discrepancy between known anatomy and tracing results.

claim: Descending serotonergic projections of the hindbrain are particularly challenging to study using currently available tools.
source: Together these reports would suggest that descending serotonergic projections of the hindbrain are particularly challenging to study using the currently available tools.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited literature showing limitations of viral tracers.

claim: Following intraspinal injection of AAV2retro.GFP, many transduced neurons were labeled within the RVM.
source: Following intraspinal injection of AAV2retro.GFP, many transduced neurons were labeled within the RVM (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the image shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The majority of eGFP and TPH2 double-positive cells were located within the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi).
source: When we inspected the location of neurons that expressed both TPH2 and eGFP (according to scheme depicted in Figure 1—figure supplement 1), we found that the majority of these cells were located within the lateral paragigantocellularis (LPGi) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification and images shown in Figure 1.

claim: 74% of eGFP-labeled TPH2-expressing neurons were in the LPGi both ipsilateral and contralateral to the spinal cord injection site.
source: Quantification of the location of the eGFP-labeled TPH2-expressing neurons indicated that 74% were in the LPGi both ipsilateral and contralateral to the spinal cord injection site (left hand side).
evidence: This is a quantification of the anatomical tracing data.

claim: Far fewer eGFP + TPH2+ neurons were found within the midline serotonergic nuclei (23/100 neurons in NRM).
source: In agreement with (Wang et al., 2018), far fewer eGFP + TPH2+neurons were found within the midline serotonergic nuclei 23/100 neurons in NRM, (n=3 animals; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantification of the anatomical tracing data, supported by a citation.

claim: Most non-serotonergic projection neurons (eGFP + TPH2-) were found close to the midline of the ventral hindbrain (412/439 neurons in midline).
source: However, most non-serotonergic projection neurons (eGFP + TPH2-) were found close to the midline of the ventral hindbrain 412/439 neurons in midline, (n=3 animals; see Figure 1B and Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantification of the anatomical tracing data.

claim: Many CTb-labeled TPH2-expressing hindbrain neurons were found in the midline NRM.
source: Strikingly, many CTb-labeled TPH2-expressing hindbrain neurons were found in the midline NRM, although CTb-containing TPH2-expressing neurons were also found in the LPGi (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The location of CTb + TPH2 + cells was more evenly divided between the NRM and LPGi than the eGFP + TPH2 + cells from the AAV2retro labeling.
source: The location of these CTb + TPH2 + cells was more evenly divided between the NRM and LPGi that the eGFP + TPH2 + cells from the AAV2retro labeling (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C compared to Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a comparison of quantitative data from two different tracing methods.

claim: More neurons in the ventral hindbrain were retrogradely labeled with CTb than AAV2retro.eGFP.
source: In total, more neurons in the ventral hindbrain were retrogradely labeled with CTb than AAV2retro.eGFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification shown in the figure supplement and table.

claim: Far fewer TPH2-expressing retrogradely labeled neurons were labelled with AAV2retro.GFP relative to the overall population of traced neurons.
source: When only TPH2-expressing retrogradely labeled neurons were examined, far fewer were labelled with AAV2retro.GFP relative to the overall population of traced neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification shown in the figure supplement and table.

claim: A lower percentage of neurons in the medial serotonergic nuclei including the NRM were labeled with eGFP compared to the LPGi.
source: However, when the retrogradely labeled TPH2 + neurons were divided into separate areas, it was apparent that a lower percentage of neurons in the medial serotonergic nuclei including the NRM were labeled with eGFP compared to the LPGi, whereas the proportion of serotonergic neurons in the LPGi labeled with AAV2retro, CTb, and both AAV2retro and CTb were similar to the general population of retrogradely labeled hindbrain neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This is supported by the quantification shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The reduced labeling of hindbrain serotonergic neurons with AAV2retro was due to a resistance of midline serotonergic neurons to AAV2retro-mediated transduction.
source: Therefore, we conclude that the reduced labeling of hindbrain serotonergic neurons with AAV2retro was due to a resistance of midline serotonergic neurons to AAV2retro-mediated transduction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative tracing data.

claim: Laterally located serotonergic neurons were more amenable to retrograde transduction with AAV2retro.
source: In contrast, laterally located serotonergic neurons were more amenable to retrograde transduction with AAV2retro.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative tracing data.

claim: 44% of the labeled hindbrain neurons contained detectable TPH2 immunoreactivity 5 days after injection of SAD.rabΔG-eGFP (SAD-G).
source: Five days after injection of SAD.rabΔG-eGFP (SAD-G), 44% of the labeled hindbrain neurons contained detectable TPH2 immunoreactivity (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B, C).
evidence: This is a quantification of the rabies tracing data.

claim: The percentage of labeled neurons expressing TPH2 dropped to only 12% at day 7 post injection of rabies virus.
source: Notably, the percentage of labeled neurons dropped to only 12% of labeled hindbrain neurons at day 7 post injection (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is a quantification of the rabies tracing data at a different time point.

claim: The reduction in TPH2-positive labeled neurons at day 7 may be a result of rabies virus toxicity.
source: This reduction may be a result of rabies virus toxicity, which could lead to a downregulation of cytoplasmic enzymes such as TPH2 to undetectable levels, and hence an underestimation of labeled serotonergic neurons.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed reduction.

claim: Only 3% of eGFP-labeled hindbrain neurons from transsynaptic tracing expressed TPH2.
source: We only observed coexpression of eGFP and TPH2 once in a total of 33 inspected neurons, corresponding to 3% of our total sample (Figure 1—figure supplement 4E, F).
evidence: This is a quantification of the transsynaptic rabies tracing data.

claim: All eGFP-expressing neurons in the hindbrain were transsynaptically traced from the dorsal horn.
source: In the hindbrain, we never observed colocalization of mCherry and eGFP, suggesting that all eGFP-expressing neurons in the hindbrain were transsynaptically traced from the dorsal horn.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of double-labeled neurons.

claim: The lack of transsynaptic labeling from the dorsal horn is possibly due to the synaptic organization of serotonergic axons at this site.
source: The lack of transsynaptic labeling from the dorsal horn is possibly due to the synaptic organization of serotonergic axons at this site, since serotonin is known to mainly act via volume transmission (Ridet et al., 1993).
evidence: This is speculation supported by a citation about serotonin transmission.

claim: Most serotonergic axons in the rat dorsal horn do not form synaptic contacts.
source: Most serotonergic axons in the rat dorsal horn do not form synaptic contacts (Maxwell et al., 1983; Ridet et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Some 5-HT-containing axonal boutons do form synapses within the dorsal horn, and these are observed as symmetrical synapses.
source: However, some 5-HT-containing axonal boutons do form synapses within the dorsal horn, and these are observed as symmetrical synapses (Polgár et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Tph2-Cre is expressed specifically in serotonergic neurons among the hindbrain neurons that project to the spinal dorsal horn.
source: Therefore, among the hindbrain neurons that project to the spinal dorsal horn Tph2-Cre is expressed specifically in serotonergic neurons, but may also be expressed in other neurons of the nervous system, including a subset of DRG neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the quantification showing high colocalization of eGFP and TPH2 in hindbrain projection neurons.

claim: Tph2-Cre may also be expressed in other neurons of the nervous system, including a subset of DRG neurons.
source: Therefore, among the hindbrain neurons that project to the spinal dorsal horn Tph2-Cre is expressed specifically in serotonergic neurons, but may also be expressed in other neurons of the nervous system, including a subset of DRG neurons.
evidence: This is supported by the observation of labeled DRG neurons in the tracing experiments.

claim: 72% of eGFP neurons from AAV2retro.flex.eGFP labeling were present bilaterally in the LPGi.
source: We observed a similar pattern in cell location as in the AAV2retro.eGFP labeling experiments (Figure 1C), with 72% of eGFP neurons being present bilaterally in the LPGi (Figure 2D and Table 3).
evidence: This is a quantification of the anatomical tracing data.

claim: 77.5% of all neurons labeled with AAV2retro.flex.eGFP contained detectable levels of TPH2.
source: Furthermore, 77.5% of all neurons labeled with AAV2retro.flex.eGFP contained detectable levels of TPH2 (Figure 2E and Table 3).
evidence: This is a quantification of the anatomical tracing data.

claim: 80.6% of all retrogradely transduced neurons were labeled with eGFP using the intersectional strategy.
source: With this approach, we labeled 80.6% of all retrogradely transduced neurons with eGFP with the remaining 19.4% containing mCherry only, indicating that most retrogradely transduced neurons are labeled using this strategy (Figure 2H and Table 4).
evidence: This is a quantification of the intersectional labeling efficiency.

claim: The proportion of retrogradely labeled neurons captured by the hindbrain injection was similar between different areas containing retrogradely labeled serotonergic neurons.
source: Additionally, this proportion was similar between the different areas containing retrogradely labeled serotonergic neurons (LPGi = 80.6%, Medial = 78.3%, other = 82.4%, labeled neurons containing eGFP), suggesting these injection sites encompass most regions that contain AAV2retro-labeled serotonergic projection neurons.
evidence: This is a quantification and interpretation of the intersectional labeling data.

claim: A smaller proportion of eGFP-only neurons were present in the LPGi compared to the medial serotonergic nuclei (4.6% vs 16.9% respectively).
source: We found that a smaller proportion of eGFP-only neurons were present in the LPGi compared to the medial serotonergic nuclei (4.6% vs 16.9% respectively, Figure 2H and Table 4).
evidence: This is a quantification of the intersectional labeling data.

claim: The intersectional strategy is suitable for the specific manipulation of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that project to the spinal dorsal horn.
source: We concluded that this intersectional strategy is suitable for the specific manipulation of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that project to the spinal dorsal horn, and that the majority of these traced cells are located in the LPGi.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the intersectional labeling data.

claim: The majority of intersectionally traced cells are located in the LPGi.
source: We concluded that this intersectional strategy is suitable for the specific manipulation of serotonergic hindbrain neurons that project to the spinal dorsal horn, and that the majority of these traced cells are located in the LPGi.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the intersectional labeling data.

claim: Within the RVM, the innervation of the superficial dorsal horn originates from the lateral hindbrain.
source: Previous anterograde tracing studies have suggested that within the RVM, the innervation of the superficial dorsal horn originates from the lateral hindbrain, whereas the deeper dorsal horn is innervated by the medial hindbrain (Gautier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The deeper dorsal horn is innervated by the medial hindbrain.
source: Previous anterograde tracing studies have suggested that within the RVM, the innervation of the superficial dorsal horn originates from the lateral hindbrain, whereas the deeper dorsal horn is innervated by the medial hindbrain (Gautier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 80.5% of eGFP-labeled neurons in the NRM injection site contained a detectable level of TPH2.
source: Most eGFP-labeled neurons in the injection site contained a detectable level of TPH2 (80.5%), indicating this strategy can be used to label the serotonergic midline neurons of the hindbrain (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a quantification of the labeling specificity.

claim: The densest labelling of axon terminals from LPGi neurons was present in the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn.
source: The intersectional approach revealed that the densest labelling of axon terminals was present in the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn (Figure 3D, E and H).
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing images.

claim: Most of the labeled axons from LPGi neurons were seen within the dorsal CGRP plexus, indicating that these neurons innervate laminae I-IIo of the spinal cord.
source: When the spinal cords were immunostained for CGRP and PKCγ (to delineate laminae I-IIo and IIi boundaries, respectively), most of the labeled axons were seen within the dorsal CGRP plexus, indicating that these neurons innervate laminae I-IIo of the spinal cord (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data showing laminar localization.

claim: Descending neurons from LPGi have a wide-ranging axon termination pattern that extends over most of the spinal cord.
source: Surprisingly, projections retrogradely labeled from the left lumbar spinal cord contained axon collaterals that projected to both ipsilateral and contralateral dorsal horns, as well as to spinal segments caudal to the spinal injection site in the lumbar segment (Figure 3E and H). This indicates that these descending neurons have a wide-ranging axon termination pattern that extends over most of the spinal cord.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical tracing data.

claim: Axons from midline serotonergic neurons were rarely present in the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn, but they densely innervated the ventral horn and were present in the deep dorsal horn.
source: In contrast, axons from midline serotonergic neurons (including NRM, ROb, and RPa) directly labeled with tdTomato (from injection of AAVs containing a Cre-dependent tdTOM [AAV8.flex.tdTOM] into the NRM [–6, 0, 5.9]) were rarely present in the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn, but they densely innervated the ventral horn and were present in the deep dorsal horn (Figure 3G, I).
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing images.

claim: The axons of medial serotonergic neurons were mostly present ventral to the lamina IIi-III border.
source: This was confirmed by revealing the laminar boundaries with CGRP and PKCγ staining, which indicated that the axons of these neurons was mostly present ventral to the lamina IIi-III border (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data showing laminar localization.

claim: Most of the axon terminals in the spinal cord from both LPGi and medial neurons contained 5-HT.
source: In both labeling experiments, most of the axon terminals in the spinal cord contained 5-HT, although much of the spinal 5-HT was not colocalized with tdTomato by either labeling approach (Figure 3H, I).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data.

claim: Much of the spinal 5-HT was not colocalized with tdTomato by either labeling approach.
source: In both labeling experiments, most of the axon terminals in the spinal cord contained 5-HT, although much of the spinal 5-HT was not colocalized with tdTomato by either labeling approach (Figure 3H, I).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data.

claim: The lateral and midline serotonergic neurons in the RVM project to distinct regions of the spinal cord.
source: Together this indicates that the lateral and midline serotonergic neurons in the RVM project to distinct regions of the spinal cord, in agreement with Gautier et al., 2017.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the anatomical tracing data, supported by a citation.

claim: Tph2-Cre neurons in the LPGi and NRM had similar active membrane properties and neuronal excitability.
source: In contrast to their anatomical differences (such as cell soma location and spinal axon termination pattern), Tph2-Cre neurons in the LPGi and NRM had similar active membrane properties and neuronal excitability (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4.

claim: LPGi and NRM neurons discharged action potentials that were similar in terms of their thresholds, kinetics, and firing rates.
source: In response to depolarizing current steps, these two groups of neurons discharged action potentials that were similar in terms of their thresholds, kinetics, and firing rates (Figure 4A, B and D–G).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiological data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Both LPGi and NRM serotonergic neurons generally had broad action potentials.
source: Similar to previous reports on the electrophysiological properties of serotonergic RVM neurons, both groups generally had broad action potentials (measured as width at half maximal) and frequently exhibited a slow afterhyperpolarization (9/10 NRM neurons, 5/8 LPGi neurons), which was similar in amplitude between groups (Figure 4A, E and H; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiological data and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Both LPGi and NRM serotonergic neurons frequently exhibited a slow afterhyperpolarization (9/10 NRM neurons, 5/8 LPGi neurons).
source: Similar to previous reports on the electrophysiological properties of serotonergic RVM neurons, both groups generally had broad action potentials (measured as width at half maximal) and frequently exhibited a slow afterhyperpolarization (9/10 NRM neurons, 5/8 LPGi neurons), which was similar in amplitude between groups (Figure 4A, E and H; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a quantification of the electrophysiological data.

claim: The slow afterhyperpolarization was similar in amplitude between LPGi and NRM groups.
source: Similar to previous reports on the electrophysiological properties of serotonergic RVM neurons, both groups generally had broad action potentials (measured as width at half maximal) and frequently exhibited a slow afterhyperpolarization (9/10 NRM neurons, 5/8 LPGi neurons), which was similar in amplitude between groups (Figure 4A, E and H; Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by the electrophysiological data.

claim: Optogenetic activation of serotonergic neurons of the NRM produces long-term hypersensitivity to both mechanical and thermal sensitivity.
source: Descending serotonergic projection neurons can both decrease or increase pain sensitivity, and optogenetic activation of serotonergic neurons of the NRM produces long-term hypersensitivity to both mechanical and thermal sensitivity (Cai et al., 2014; Wei et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Intrathecal injection of serotonin can produce acute antinociception.
source: However, intrathecal injection of serotonin can produce acute antinociception (Wang, 1977), and currently little is known of the effect of preferentially activating descending serotonergic neurons in the LPGi.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Virtually all mCherry-expressing axon terminals in the lumbar spinal cord from LPGi activation experiments contained detectable 5-HT.
source: Although many neurons of the hindbrain were labeled with hM3Dq-mCherry and virtually all mCherry-expressing axon terminals in the lumbar spinal cord contained detectable 5-HT, this only corresponded to a minority of the serotonergic innervation in this area (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The labeled terminals from LPGi activation experiments only corresponded to a minority of the serotonergic innervation in the lumbar spinal cord.
source: Although many neurons of the hindbrain were labeled with hM3Dq-mCherry and virtually all mCherry-expressing axon terminals in the lumbar spinal cord contained detectable 5-HT, this only corresponded to a minority of the serotonergic innervation in this area (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data shown in Figure 5.

claim: After injecting CNO, hM3Dq-mCherry-expressing neurons increased their activity, as evidenced by an increased expression of c-Fos in their nuclei relative to vehicle injected controls.
source: After injecting CNO hM3Dq-mCherry-expressing neurons increased their activity, as evidenced by an increased expression of c-Fos in their nuclei relative to vehicle injected controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the c-Fos immunostaining data shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Withdrawal latencies to thermal stimuli were increased following CNO injection in LPGi activation experiments.
source: Despite sparse terminal labeling in the spinal cord, withdrawal latencies to thermal stimuli were increased following CNO injection (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Animals that had received CNO injections exhibited significantly longer withdrawal thresholds to infrared heat stimulation than vehicle injected controls (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 9)=10.55, p<0.0001).
source: Animals that had received CNO injections exhibited significantly longer withdrawal thresholds to infrared heat stimulation than vehicle injected controls (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 9)=10.55, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Response latencies to the cold plantar assay were prolonged following CNO injection in LPGi activation experiments (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 9)=7.309, p=0.0012).
source: Similarly, response latencies to the cold plantar assay were also prolonged following CNO injection (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 9)=7.309, p=0.0012).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Tactile sensitivity to punctate mechanical stimulation with von Frey filaments was unaltered in LPGi activation experiments (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 9)=1.402, p=0.2666).
source: In contrast, tactile sensitivity to punctate mechanical stimulation with von Frey filaments was unaltered (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 9)=1.402, p=0.2666) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Latency to fall from an accelerating rotarod was comparable between animals before and after CNO injection in LPGi activation experiments (repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 5)=0.354, p=0.787).
source: Latency to fall was comparable between animals before and after injection indicating no deficits in sensorimotor function or the absence of sedative effects (repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 5)=0.354, p=0.787; Figure 5D)
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Acute activation of descending serotonergic neurons reduces sensitivity to thermal stimuli, but does not strongly influence mechanical sensitivity.
source: Together, these data indicate that acute activation of descending serotonergic neurons reduces sensitivity to thermal stimuli, but does not strongly influence mechanical sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data.

claim: A significant increase in withdrawal latencies to heat stimulation was seen in the contralateral paw in the Hargreaves assay (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 14)=7.757, p=0.0003).
source: We saw a significant increase in withdrawal latencies to heat stimulation in the Hargreaves assay (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 14)=7.757, p=0.0003; Figure 5—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data from the contralateral paw.

claim: The activation of LPGi neurons has some influence on the sensitivity of the contralateral paw, presumably via axon collaterals present in the contralateral dorsal horn.
source: The presence of axon collaterals on the contralateral side of the spinal cord raises the possibility that these could also mediate a similar effect to those on the ipsilateral side. Therefore, we also tested the contralateral paw using the same sensory tests (Figure 5—figure supplement 2). We saw a significant increase in withdrawal latencies to heat stimulation in the Hargreaves assay (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 14)=7.757, p=0.0003; Figure 5—figure supplement 3), suggesting that the activation of these neurons has some influence on the sensitivity of the contralateral paw, presumably via axon collaterals present in the contralateral dorsal horn.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical and behavioral data.

claim: Both male and female mice show reduced sensitivity to thermal stimuli following LPGi activation.
source: To see if similar differences are observed in our experiment, we divided the group into male and female animals to determine whether both sexes responded in a similar manner. We find that both male and female mice show reduced sensitivity to thermal stimuli, and both show unaltered mechanical sensitivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data divided by sex.

claim: Both male and female mice show unaltered mechanical sensitivity following LPGi activation.
source: We find that both male and female mice show reduced sensitivity to thermal stimuli, and both show unaltered mechanical sensitivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data divided by sex.

claim: The injection of CNO did not produce any noticeable change in any of the behavioral tests in the absence of hM3Dq expression.
source: In addition, CNO has been reported to mediate effects independently of hM3Dq expression (Gomez et al., 2017). To exclude that the effects seen in our assays were caused by such off-target effects, we performed the same sensory and motor tests on animals that did not express hM3Dq. In our hands, the injection of CNO did not produce any noticeable change in any of the behavioral tests in the absence of hM3Dq expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a control experiment to rule out off-target effects of CNO.

claim: On average, 67% of BFP-labeled neurons were also labeled with hM3Dq-mCherry in LPGi activation experiments.
source: When we examined the hindbrain tissues from animals used in the LPGi activation experiments, we quantified the proportion of retrogradely labeled and intersectionally labeled neurons. On average, 67% of BFP-labeled neurons were also labeled with hM3Dq-mCherry, and very few (1.85%) only expressed mCherry (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a quantification of the labeling specificity.

claim: Very few neurons (1.85%) only expressed mCherry in LPGi activation experiments.
source: On average, 67% of BFP-labeled neurons were also labeled with hM3Dq-mCherry, and very few (1.85%) only expressed mCherry (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a quantification of the labeling specificity.

claim: The intersectional strategy employed for chemogenetic activation of descending serotonergic neurons is similarly specific as the previous labeling experiments.
source: This shows that the intersectional strategy employed for chemogenetic activation of descending serotonergic neurons is similarly specific as our previous labeling experiments (Figure 2F, G and H).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantification of labeled neurons.

claim: Activation of serotonergic neurons has been associated with increased sensitivity to tactile and thermal stimuli.
source: Activation of serotonergic neurons has also been associated with increased sensitivity to tactile and thermal stimuli and is thought to underly certain forms of neuropathic pain (Cai et al., 2014; Suzuki et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Activation of serotonergic neurons is thought to underly certain forms of neuropathic pain.
source: Activation of serotonergic neurons has also been associated with increased sensitivity to tactile and thermal stimuli and is thought to underly certain forms of neuropathic pain (Cai et al., 2014; Suzuki et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: mCherry-labeled terminals from medial neuron activation were located in the deep dorsal horn of the spinal cord, with limited expression in the dense plexus of 5-HT terminals in the superficial spinal laminae.
source: This resulted in the presence of mCherry-labeled terminals in the deep dorsal horn of the spinal cord, with limited expression in the dense plexus of 5-HT terminals in the superficial spinal laminae (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Activation of medial RVM neurons had no effect on thermal withdrawal latencies (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=0.531, p=0.667).
source: In contrast to the activation of serotonergic neurons within the LPGi, the activation of medial RVM neurons had no effect on thermal withdrawal latencies (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=0.531, p=0.667) or responses to cooling (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=3.071, p=0.054; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Activation of medial RVM neurons had no effect on responses to cooling (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=3.071, p=0.054).
source: In contrast to the activation of serotonergic neurons within the LPGi, the activation of medial RVM neurons had no effect on thermal withdrawal latencies (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=0.531, p=0.667) or responses to cooling (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=3.071, p=0.054; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: A significant decrease in the withdrawal thresholds to punctate mechanical stimuli in the hindpaw was observed following activation of medial RVM neurons (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=13.84, p=0.787).
source: However, we observed a significant decrease in the withdrawal thresholds to punctate mechanical stimuli in the hindpaw (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=13.84, p=0.787; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data. Note: The p-value appears inconsistent with the claim of significance and may be a typographical error in the manuscript.

claim: Neither CNO nor vehicle injection impaired sensorimotor coordination or induced sedation in medial RVM activation experiments (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=1.791, p=0.185).
source: Again, neither CNO nor vehicle injection impaired sensorimotor coordination or induced sedation, using latency to fall from an accelerating rotarod as a readout measure (Repeated measures one-way ANOVA, F(3, 6)=1.791, p=0.185; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the behavioral data.

claim: Activating medial serotonergic hindbrain neurons increases mechanical sensitivity without influencing responses to thermal stimuli.
source: These data indicate that, in contrast to serotonergic neurons of the LPGi, activating medial serotonergic hindbrain neurons increases mechanical sensitivity without influencing responses to thermal stimuli.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral data.

claim: Both male and female animals exhibit similar increases in mechanical sensitivity after CNO injection in medial RVM activation experiments.
source: To test for potential sex differences in mechanical hypersensitivity, we again divided our group into males and females and compared the withdrawal thresholds/latencies post-vehicle injection to post-CNO injection. We see that both male and female animals exhibit similar increases in mechanical sensitivity after CNO injection (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), suggesting that this effect is not sex specific.
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral data divided by sex.

claim: The mechanical hypersensitivity effect from medial RVM activation is not sex specific.
source: We see that both male and female animals exhibit similar increases in mechanical sensitivity after CNO injection (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), suggesting that this effect is not sex specific.
evidence: This is an inference based on the behavioral data showing similar effects in both sexes.

claim: A similar proportion of neurons (85.1%) expressed TPH2 in the medial hindbrain injection sites from behavioral experiments as compared to previous labeling experiments.
source: Additionally, when we inspected the injection sites in the brain stem from animals used in these behavioral experiments, we found that a similar proportion of neurons expressed TPH2 (85.1%, Figure 6—figure supplement 3) as compared to our previous labeling experiments (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a quantification of the labeling specificity.

claim: The chemogenetic activation is largely restricted to serotonergic neurons of the medial hindbrain in the medial RVM activation experiments.
source: Therefore, we concluded that the chemogenetic activation is largely restricted to serotonergic neurons of the medial hindbrain in these experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantification of TPH2 expression in labeled neurons.

claim: The same transmitter released into different spinal laminae can produce opposing effects on spinal nociception.
source: Together the results of the chemogenetic experiments indicate that the same transmitter released into different spinal laminae can produce opposing effects on spinal nociception.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined behavioral and anatomical data.

claim: Potential explanations for the opposing effects include the 5-HTR subtypes that are engaged, the spinal neuron populations that are modulated, or a combination of both.
source: Potential explanations for these findings include the 5-HTR subtypes that are engaged, the spinal neuron populations that are modulated, or a combination of both.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanisms underlying the observed effects.

claim: Some 5-HTRs are known to have an excitatory influence when activated, whereas others have an inhibitory effect upon ligand binding.
source: Some 5-HTRs are known to have an excitatory influence when activated, whereas others have an inhibitory effect upon ligand binding (Abe et al., 2009; Bardoni, 2019; Lu and Perl, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The activation of excitatory neurons and the inhibition of inhibitory neurons in the deep dorsal horn are known to increase mechanical sensitivity.
source: The activation of excitatory neurons and the inhibition of inhibitory neurons in the deep dorsal horn, corresponding to the termination zone of the medial serotonergic neurons, are known increase mechanical sensitivity (Duan et al., 2014; Foster et al., 2015; Peirs et al., 2021; Peirs et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The activation of inhibitory neurons in the superficial dorsal horn could promote thermal hyposensitivity.
source: Conversely, the activation of inhibitory neurons in the superficial dorsal horn, the region innervated by the lateral serotonergic neurons, and the inhibition of nociceptors through presynaptic inhibition of their central terminals could promote thermal hyposensitivity (Jeong et al., 2012; Lu and Perl, 2007; Xie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The inhibition of nociceptors through presynaptic inhibition of their central terminals could promote thermal hyposensitivity.
source: Conversely, the activation of inhibitory neurons in the superficial dorsal horn, the region innervated by the lateral serotonergic neurons, and the inhibition of nociceptors through presynaptic inhibition of their central terminals could promote thermal hyposensitivity (Jeong et al., 2012; Lu and Perl, 2007; Xie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Surprisingly little difference was found in the passive and active membrane properties between NRM and LPGi serotonergic neurons.
source: Given the previously reported heterogeneity in biophysical properties of serotonergic neurons (Okaty et al., 2019), we found surprisingly little difference in the passive and active membrane properties between NRM and LPGi serotonergic neurons (Table 5 and Figure 4).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the electrophysiological data, with a citation to previous literature.

claim: None of the recorded neurons displayed spontaneous activity.
source: Additionally, none of the recorded neurons displayed spontaneous activity, which has been reported previously for serotonergic projection neurons of the hindbrain (Zhang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an observation from the electrophysiological recordings, with a citation to previous literature.

claim: The lack of spontaneous activity may be attributable to differences in recording conditions.
source: This may be attributable to differences in recording conditions, such as recording temperature, animal species, and recording solution composition.
evidence: This is speculation about the reasons for the discrepancy with previous literature.

claim: Serotonergic neurons of the lateral hindbrain are antinociceptive when activated.
source: Primarily, our data demonstrate that serotonergic neurons of the lateral hindbrain are antinociceptive when activated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the chemogenetic activation experiments.

claim: Lateral hindbrain serotonergic neurons project their axons to the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn.
source: These neurons project their axons to the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn and can be targeted using AAV2retro vectors.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing data.

claim: Lateral hindbrain serotonergic neurons can be targeted using AAV2retro vectors.
source: These neurons project their axons to the superficial laminae of the dorsal horn and can be targeted using AAV2retro vectors.
evidence: This is supported by the tracing data showing preferential transduction.

claim: The medial serotonergic neurons are largely resistant to AAV2retro-mediated transduction.
source: In contrast, the medial serotonergic neurons are largely resistant to AAV2retro-mediated transduction, produce mechanical hypersensitivity upon acute activation, and project their axons to the deeper dorsal horn.
evidence: This is supported by the comparative tracing data.

claim: Medial serotonergic neurons produce mechanical hypersensitivity upon acute activation.
source: In contrast, the medial serotonergic neurons are largely resistant to AAV2retro-mediated transduction, produce mechanical hypersensitivity upon acute activation, and project their axons to the deeper dorsal horn.
evidence: This is supported by the chemogenetic activation experiments.

claim: Medial serotonergic neurons project their axons to the deeper dorsal horn.
source: In contrast, the medial serotonergic neurons are largely resistant to AAV2retro-mediated transduction, produce mechanical hypersensitivity upon acute activation, and project their axons to the deeper dorsal horn.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical tracing data.

claim: The limitations of AAV2retro-mediated and rabies-virus-based transsynaptic tracing from the spinal dorsal horn are likely to have broader implications for transsynaptic rabies-based circuit tracing and the targeting of other projections that use biogenic amines.
source: Secondly, we highlight some of the limitations and challenges associated with AAV2retro-mediated and rabies-virus-based transsynaptic tracing from the spinal dorsal horn. These limitations are likely to have broader implications for transsynaptic rabies-based circuit tracing and the targeting of other projections that use biogenic amines, and possibly other transmitter systems.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tracing experiments, with implications for future studies.
